diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: A video on social media shows that the principal of Mahd Elm School in Riz, Bushehr, after a student refused to throw his mobile phone into a bucket of water, hit the student's hand and threw the phone into the bucket. The images indicate injury to the student's hand.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Trump administration currently has intensifying economic pressure and isolation of the Islamic Republic on its agenda, and the simultaneous increase of US military presence in the region also maintains a shadow of military threat over the regime. According to him, Trump, with this strategy, alongside pressure on the regime, is waiting for the economic and social consequences inside Iran and the people's reaction to the current conditions.

France announced that on Monday it will present evidence of a cyberattack attributed to the IRGC targeting refrigerators in food stores in the country to European ministers and will call for new sanctions against Tehran. Jean-Noël Barrot, French Foreign Minister, said Paris aims to prepare a list of new individuals and entities for sanctions within a month.

Mahmoud Nabavian, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, criticized the negotiation plan with the US, saying it does not specify who the "aggressor" is. He questioned whether the death of Ali Khamenei was accidental or an act of aggression. Nabavian added that without identifying the aggressor, the cases of punishing the aggressor and revenge will be closed, and he asked officials why they no longer talk about revenge.
A video published on social media shows that rainfall caused flooding and the entry of floodwaters into Mazgah village in Nowshahr on Monday, 25 Aban.

Romelu Lukaku, the 33-year-old striker of the Belgium national team and Fenerbahçe club, suddenly announced his retirement from international football after 16 years. He wrote on Instagram that he enjoyed every moment of this adventure and thanked his teammates, coaches, and fans. Lukaku ended his international career with 135 appearances and 94 goals, becoming the top scorer in Belgium's national team history.
Today, continuing the gatherings of telecommunications retirees; some of these retirees in the cities of Tehran and Isfahan also held a protest gathering demanding attention to their demands.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International on Monday, 25 Aban, showing a queue of cars waiting for gasoline on one of the roads leading to Bushehr, stating that most gas stations did not have gasoline cards and only one station had one card.
A video sent to Iran International on Monday, 25 Aban, shows severe air pollution in Tehran. According to the video, a thick black haze has enveloped the city like a shadow.

Jean-Noël Barrot, French Foreign Minister, said France was likely targeted by a cyberattack on cooling systems in stores because it has consistently supported the Iranian people against the Islamic Republic's repression. He held the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps responsible and said France submitted files with evidence about the main perpetrators to the European Union, requesting sanctions within one month. Barrot added that broad support was gained at the EU foreign ministers' meeting for these sanctions and he hopes they will be approved at the December 14 meeting.

Jean-Noël Barrot, French Foreign Minister, said many of his counterparts in the European Union support new sanctions. He described these sanctions as a response to France's support for the Iranian people after the killing of protesters in Dey month. Barrot added that Paris proposed sanctions against individuals and entities linked to the IRGC to the EU following cyberattacks on more than 700 retail centers in France.

On Sunday, 24 Aban, the homes of five Bahá'í families in Semnan were searched and three individuals were arrested. Intelligence officers arrested Behfar Khanjani, Hesam Tabianian, and Zohreh Nikayin, and personal belongings and electronic equipment were confiscated. The residences of Leida Pirasteh and her husband, as well as Babak and Parvaneh Shabirian, were also searched.

The son of a 50-year-old Shush municipality worker says his father fell while working with a lift and suffered a brain injury. He claims the lift had no safety features and parts of its body were rotten.

Ebrahim Rezaei, a member of the Parliament's National Security Commission, said that all enemy scenarios including war, assassination, and heliborne attacks must be thwarted and the armed forces are capable of handling them. He added that the enemy must be made to understand that the nation will not surrender to economic pressure, sanctions, assassination, or military attack. These statements were made on Monday, 25 Aban.

The Israeli army announced that in the Thursday attack on Nasser Hospital in the Gaza Strip, several members of Hamas's military wing were killed, one of whom participated in the abduction of Adina Moshe. The army said Hamas had presented the killed as civilians, but investigations show they were members of the military wing. The target of the attack was a room and floor of the hospital used by senior Hamas commanders as a military command center, where civilians were forbidden to enter.

A court in Bahrain on Tuesday, 25 Aban, sentenced 64 Shia citizens, including 57 clerics, to life imprisonment on charges related to "terrorism" and connections with the IRGC. Bahraini authorities accused the defendants of "forming a terrorist group, cooperating with the IRGC, and attempting to overthrow the ruling system" of the country.

Amir Ghalenoei, head coach of Iran's national football team, criticized the short interval between matches and the condition of the playing field before the match against Iraq in the Basra international tournament, stating that the main goal of the national team is youth development, not achieving results. Ghalenoei said the interval between Iran's match with Palestine and the match with Iraq is shorter than the interval between Iraq's match with Lebanon and their match with Iran, which prevents the team from having proper tactical training. He also pointed out that holding two matches in one day on the same field will negatively affect the second match.

Carlo Ancelotti, the coach of Brazil's national team, responded to Romario's call for his dismissal by saying that Romario talks a lot but has the right to express his opinion. Ancelotti admitted that his team's performance is not yet satisfactory and emphasized that the team is in the phase of testing new players. He expressed satisfaction with the evaluation of players such as Gabriel Bontempo, Andre, and Jonathan Jesus.

Jean-Noël Barrot, France's Foreign Minister, said he will present evidence of Iran's involvement in cyberattacks on French store refrigerators to European diplomats. He hopes new sanctions against Iran for these attacks will be approved in mid-December. Iran's Foreign Ministry and the Revolutionary Guards deny the accusations and call it a false flag operation by Israel.

Alireza Zakani, mayor of Tehran, announced that in over five years, not a single meeting has been held to address the capital's air pollution problem. He emphasized that 23 agencies are involved in the air pollution issue and the municipality is only one of them. Zakani attributed the responsibility for holding meetings to other institutions and said a major part of Tehran's air pollution comes from activities around the capital.

Reuters reported, citing Iraqi officials, that Kata'ib Hezbollah, one of the most powerful armed groups supported by the Islamic Republic in Iraq, has earned hundreds of millions of dollars through an oil smuggling network. According to security and oil officials, this network has operated since 2021 with the cooperation of some government officials, and investigations have led to the dismissal of 9 senior officials. Ali Al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, has ordered the deployment of more forces around the Jurf al-Sakhar area.
Mahnaz Ebrahimi, a math teacher and teachers' union activist in Shiraz, was released from Adelabad prison in Shiraz on Sunday, 24 Aban, on bail. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

The war in Iran and disruptions in oil tanker passage through the Strait of Hormuz have cast a shadow over the ASEAN summit in Manila. Eleven Southeast Asian countries and their partners face rising energy and transportation costs and demand guarantees for the safe passage of ships through this route.

Some viewers of Iran International said the suppression of protesters in Aban 98 ended their hope for reforming the Islamic Republic. Others said the experience deepened their opposition to the government. Viewers mentioned internet shutdowns, shooting protesters, arrests, and commemorated the martyrs of Aban.

The director general of forensic medicine in Semnan province announced that from the beginning of this year until the end of Mehr, 236 people died and 4255 were injured in traffic accidents in this province. The number of injured increased by 2% and the number of deaths by 11% compared to the same period last year. Among the deceased, 207 died in intercity accidents, 23 in urban accidents, and six on rural roads.

A video sent to Iran International shows a large presence of security motorcyclists on Neshat Street in Isfahan on Tuesday, 25 Aban. According to reports, the area of this street has been heavily secured with checkpoints and armed individuals.

Mohammad Sajjad Shahdoust, a detainee related to the December 1404 protests, is serving his two-year sentence in Tehran Grand Prison. He was transferred to prison on 16 Aban. The Revolutionary Court sentenced him on charges of "disturbing public order" and "propaganda against the regime."

Zohreh Sadat Lajevardi, Tehran's parliamentary representative, said that women's motorcycling is "not our main priority" and that livelihood problems and the situation of female heads of households should be addressed. She added that issuing licenses for women's motorcycling should be examined considering its "requirements" such as potential dangers and how women dress while motorcycling.

Alireza Dabir told Fars news agency that those who asked why forces go to Syria now understand the reason for their presence. He said the city council allocated a budget in 1386 for building Iranian Park in southern Lebanon and discussed the spending with Qasem Soleimani. According to Dabir, Soleimani laughed and said 3 billion tomans is a small amount because the forces stand for Iran.

The government of Pakistan announced that Shehbaz Sharif, the Prime Minister of the country, met in Islamabad with foreign ministers and heads of delegations of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) member countries, including Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic. These officials traveled to Pakistan to attend the 30th meeting of the ECO Council of Ministers. Additionally, Muhammad Ishaq Dar, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan, held a bilateral meeting with Abbas Araghchi and emphasized that dialogue and diplomacy remain the only practical solution to resolve remaining issues, prevent escalation of tensions, and achieve lasting peace and stability.

In the eighth week of the Iranian Women's Premier Football League, Khatoon Bam defeated Persepolis 4-1. Despite this loss, Persepolis remained at the top of the table with 18 points. Esteghlal, Gol Gohar, Sepahan, and Varesh also won their matches.

Mahbubeh Ramazani, mother of Pejman Gholipour, who was killed in Aban 98, said she had no hope from the beginning for the investigation of the complaint regarding the murder of her 18-year-old son in the Islamic Republic. She added that the Islamic Republic arrests families of the killed to force them into silence. Ramazani said she is proud that her son gave his life for the freedom of Iran.

Mohammed Al-Khalifi, Qatar's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, called for strengthening guarantees to protect mediating countries, the security of negotiators, and confidentiality of diplomatic talks at the Future Resilience Forum in London. He described mediation as both an international responsibility and a national interest, highlighting Qatar's role in prisoner exchanges between the US and Venezuela and support for Colombia's peace process. Al-Khalifi also emphasized the importance of countries' credibility and ability to connect conflicting parties.
A released video shows that after rainfall on Monday, 25 Aban, flooding occurred on the ring road of Nowshahr city in Mazandaran province.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, announced that the Islamic Republic launched between 8,000 and 9,000 suicide drones and about 2,000 ballistic missiles since the start of the "Epic Anger" operation. He said only three of these drones and missiles caused American casualties. Trump described the defensive performance of the US Central Command as effective and historic.

Alireza Esteghamati, head of the Medical School at Tehran University of Medical Sciences, said the cost of diabetes treatment in Iran has increased nearly sixfold in one year. The rise in drug and equipment prices and insurance problems have made access to treatment more difficult for patients. Mehdi Beigi in today's supplement has examined the dimensions of the diabetes crisis in Iran and its consequences.
Trump said he is worried about the reporter because if he is targeted by Iranian drones, the reporter will also be harmed. He warned the reporter to be careful.

Donald Trump announced that he will discuss Iran, the Ukraine war, and nuclear disarmament in meetings with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. He also mentioned the possibility of meeting with the North Korean leader. Trump spoke about the difficulty of nuclear disarmament and the possibility of listing the Muslim Brotherhood as a terrorist organization in the US.

Mohammad Sharifimoghaddam, Secretary-General of the Nurses' House, identified staff shortages, work pressure, and livelihood problems as major factors in nurses' job burnout. He said some nurses have to care for 12 to 15 patients and during night shifts 25 to 30 patients. He also criticized the lack of a comprehensive system for monitoring nurses' physical and mental health, with consequences such as anxiety and depression.

According to a video received by Iran International, a municipal worker in the city of Shush, Khuzestan province, fell while working with a lift. In this video, recorded by the injured worker's child, the poor safety condition of the municipality's equipment and lift is highlighted.

Simultaneous with the arrival of the third US aircraft carrier near Iran, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament said Iran is on the brink of war. Also, on Sunday night, the Israeli security cabinet held a three-hour meeting with the presence of the Mossad chief about an attack on Iran.

Kaja Kallas, EU foreign policy chief, said in a November 16 press conference that cyberattacks in France indicate Europe is also targeted by Iran, and the EU is preparing more sanctions. She made these remarks regarding the Russia-Ukraine war, developments in Syria, and regional security issues. Kallas warned about Iran's reach into European countries and announced preparations for additional sanctions.

It was reported that from the beginning of Farvardin to 21 Mehr 1405, at least 84 women and girls have been killed in Iran. In 75 cases, the perpetrator was an acquaintance of the victim, and in 45 cases, the perpetrator was identified as the current or former husband, ex-husband, or romantic partner. Additionally, 12 of the victims were girls under 18 years old.

Sogand Sayadi, a 16-year-old student from Gilan-e Gharb living in Kermanshah, was killed by her father on Sunday, 24 Aban. The Hengaw Human Rights Organization reported that the cause of the killing was the father's opposition to Sogand's relationship with her suitor. The management of Rezvan Girls' High School in Kermanshah summoned Sogand's father to the school one day before the murder and he severely beat his daughter in the presence of classmates and school officials.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, stated in a conversation with Nabih Berri, the Speaker of the Lebanese Parliament, that the Islamic Republic pays special attention to Lebanon in pursuing its demands and conditions in the negotiation process. Ghalibaf said that from their perspective, without ending the war in Lebanon and achieving Lebanon's sovereignty over its territories, peace will not return to the region.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, met with Mohammad Nasir Akhund, the Taliban's Finance Minister, in Tehran. According to domestic news agencies, the two sides discussed regional issues. These talks took place while Afghanistan has become one of Iran's most important trade and transit routes.

Jean-Noël Barrot, French Foreign Minister, said Paris has been targeted by the IRGC because of its support for the Iranian people; an institution that he said the European Union considers a terrorist organization. Barrot added that France will not forget the "widespread crimes" of the IRGC against Iranians in Dey 1404.

China's Foreign Ministry announced that Xi Jinping, the President of China, will have a trilateral meeting with the leaders of the United States and Russia on Thursday in Shenzhen. It is expected that the Ukraine war, Middle East developments, Iran war, trade policies, and nuclear non-proliferation will be on the agenda of these talks. This will be the first trilateral meeting of Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin.

The Israeli army announced that its air force targeted a shipment of weapons and military equipment destined for Hezbollah in the Janta area on the Syria-Lebanon border. The army stated that the purpose of this attack was to prevent the strengthening of Hezbollah's military capabilities.
A released video shows the mother of Mohsen Abbasi expressing longing for her son by holding his clothes. Mohsen Abbasi, 21 years old, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Najafabad.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi, a political analyst, said the trilateral meeting of the US, Russia, and China could lead to an agreement on the nuclear program and regional activities of the Islamic Republic. This potential agreement includes limiting enrichment, determining the status of uranium stocks, allowing inspections by the International Atomic Energy Agency, and reducing Tehran's support for proxy groups. Namvar Haghighi added that reaching such an agreement requires mutual concessions among the three powers.

Rumors of a full-scale war returning to the Middle East have increased. Donald Trump confirmed that he will raise the issue of the Iran war at the first trilateral meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. This historic and unprecedented meeting is held among the leaders of the three great world powers.

The armed forces of southern Yemen announced that they have withdrawn from Dhubab Airport and the Bab al-Mandab area and moved towards Aden. This action was taken to secure Aden and neighboring provinces, strengthen the fronts, and confront existing threats.

Alireza Dabir, head of the Wrestling Federation, said in an interview with Fars News Agency that he is proud to belong to the Islamic Republic system and described it as Islamic. He also explained the allocation of 3 billion tomans from Tehran Municipality's budget in 2007 for building the Iranian Park in Lebanon and said Qasem Soleimani considered this amount insignificant.

Iran has enacted a law to regulate border trade aiming to provide a legal framework and improve the livelihood of border residents. The executive regulations of this law have not been fully implemented, and the gap between the law and reality persists. A joint statement by four UN special rapporteurs on September 23, 2026, has escalated this gap, shifting the issue from smuggling to violations of the right to life.

The Iran Human Rights Organization reported that 74 protesting citizens and political prisoners have been executed in about eight months, and at least 121 detainees from the Iranian National Revolution in Dey 1404 have been sentenced to death. The organization warned about the increased risk of executions of protesters ahead of the first anniversary of the Dey protests. Their report states that the execution of this number of political prisoners from 27 Esfand 1404 to 25 Aban of the current year is unprecedented since the 1360s.

The arrival of the third US aircraft carrier in the Middle East could be seen as a sign of increased pressure on Tehran. Ynet magazine wrote that upcoming developments will show whether Washington will continue its policy of maintaining the status quo and economic pressure or if the region will enter a new phase of military conflict. An interview was conducted with Farzin Nadimi, a senior defense and security researcher.

After more than three months of clashes between Houthi militias supported by the Islamic Republic and the forces of the Yemeni government and the Saudi-led coalition, the Houthis have begun advancing towards Aden following the Yemeni army's withdrawal from areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait. The Houthis now control key areas near Bab al-Mandab and, according to reports, have advanced up to 60 kilometers from Aden. This city became the seat of the Yemeni government after the Houthis captured Sana'a about a decade ago.
Mehr news agency affiliated with the Islamic Propagation Organization reported on the evening of Tuesday, 25 Aban, that air defense was activated in Isfahan.

Sogand Sayyadi, a 16-year-old student from Kermanshah, died after being transferred from school to home. It was reported that there is a possibility that this teenager was killed by her father. The prosecutor of Kermanshah announced the formation of a judicial case and the investigation of the hypotheses of murder or suicide.

In the audio version of Titrawal with Niusha Sarami, it was reported that Trump is on the way to an unprecedented meeting with Xi and Putin, and a deal regarding the Islamic Republic has been discussed.

A citizen said in a video to Iran International that the pressure from Scott Sargent, the US Treasury Secretary, is on the Iranian people. Mohsen Rezaei and Fatemeh Mohajerani said the people endure. The citizen added that people are only waiting for the destruction of the criminal Islamic Republic government.

The spokesperson for the jury of political and press courts announced that Hassan Mohammadian, the managing director of the Didar News website, and Parvaneh Salahshouri, a former member of parliament, were found guilty by the press court.

The French Foreign Ministry said in an interview with Al Arabiya on Monday, 25 Aban, that Europe is ready to participate in Iran's nuclear disarmament and that any solution regarding the Islamic Republic should also include its missile program and proxy groups. The ministry emphasized that addressing issues with Iran should not be limited to the Strait of Hormuz. It also stated that Europe seeks a fundamental resolution of problems with the Islamic Republic and is ready to participate in the process of Iran's nuclear disarmament.

Iran Shahr Street in Tehran was a popular youth hangout with cafes and nightlife until a few weeks ago. After cafes were sealed, opponents of mandatory hijab were confronted, and police forces were deployed, the street has become dominated by supporters of the Islamic Republic and their nightly gatherings. Many social media users have described this change as an effort to counter citizens' lifestyles.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, said in a meeting with Andrej Babis, Prime Minister of the Czech Republic, that Iran's missiles, terrorist actions, and nuclear ambitions are not limited to Israel's borders and that Europe is also a target of these threats. Netanyahu also criticized some European leaders and praised Babis for standing firm against terrorism. The meeting included private and broader sessions with ministers and officials from both countries.

The management of Haft-Tappeh Sugarcane told 60 official workers that if they do not sign the early retirement form, their overtime and welfare benefits will be cut. Several employees in the treatment and support departments of Iranshahr University of Medical Sciences reported unpaid months of arrears. The executive secretary of the Hormozgan Workers' House reported widespread unemployment among workers and problems receiving unemployment insurance in this province.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said on the program "Cheshmandaz" that with the arrival of the third US aircraft carrier to the region, it is still unclear whether Washington intends to strengthen its military presence and use it to pressure Tehran in negotiations or is preparing for military action. He added that officials of the Islamic Republic, regardless of the outcome of the conflict and the cost paid by the people, present themselves as victorious.

At least 10 protest gatherings were held today, Monday, 25 Aban, in the cities of Kermanshah, Sanandaj, Isfahan, Bijar, Tehran, Hamedan, Ilam, and Borujerd. Retired telecommunications workers demanded the implementation of regulation 89/24 and salary adjustments. Additionally, water drainage workers in Bandar Mahshahr and national housing applicants in Nishapur protested job uncertainty and delays in unit delivery.

The death toll from the overturning of the bus carrying employees of the Dehloran gas refinery has reached 13 with the death of another injured person. In a separate incident, three workers at a factory on the Shiraz to Jahrom route suffered gas poisoning and were transferred to the hospital.

The New York Times reported that US and Israeli airstrikes on the Islamic Republic's missile facilities raised the possibility of a connection between Iran's extensive dam and water transfer projects and the country's military needs. Seven experts told the newspaper that underground military facilities near dams could provide stable access to water and electricity for missile bases. The newspaper emphasized that due to the secrecy of Iran's missile program, this potential connection has not yet been proven.

Mahsa Nouri, a political prisoner in Evin Prison, went on a hunger strike on Monday, 25 Aban, protesting the lack of attention to her demands, including the denial of parole and refusal to grant her leave. This news was reported to Harana by a source close to her family.

The website DownDetector has recorded over 3,300 disruption reports related to Chase Bank and about 800 reports related to Bank of America and Wells Fargo. Chase Bank has confirmed issues with its online banking services and stated it is working to resolve the disruption. The fintech company Plaid announced that its connections with Chase are disrupted, affecting communication channels and API requests, and the issue is still under investigation.

In continued security pressures on Baháʼís, intelligence agents searched the homes of five Baháʼí families in Semnan and arrested three people. Also, a Baháʼí citizen in Qaemshahr was sentenced to three years in prison and eight years of deprivation of social rights, and the two-year prison sentence of another Baháʼí citizen in Tehran was confirmed. It was reported that agents arrested Khanjani after beating him and confiscated the family's phones and laptops.

The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) announced that the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt is present in the area under its command as part of a planned mission. According to CENTCOM, the aircraft carrier passed through the Indian Ocean on Sunday, November 15.

Mohammad Akraminia, spokesperson for the Islamic Republic Army, announced that the Strait of Hormuz will not return to its pre-war status and will remain closed until the United States accepts the conditions of the Islamic Republic. He said if the United States does not accept the Islamic Republic's conditions, the strait will remain closed, and the presence of foreign forces in the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman is a threat to regional security that must end. He also added that any renewed military action against the Islamic Republic will be met with a stronger response.

Varash Nowshahr defeated Palayesh Gaz Ilam 1-0 in the tenth week of the women's Premier League. With this win, Varash Nowshahr reached 9 points and moved up to sixth place in the standings. After the match, Varash Nowshahr players performed the Mazani dance.
Fardad Farahzad reported in Audio Version 24 that the largest U.S. military deployment in the Persian Gulf since the Iraq War has occurred.

The second branch of the Karaj Revolutionary Court sentenced Homayoun Shabankareh, a 22-year-old environmental activist, to death on charges of espionage. The judge issued the sentence based on confessions reportedly obtained under torture. Shabankareh was held in solitary confinement for over 130 days after being arrested by the IRGC intelligence.

Mansheh Amir, a Middle East expert, said severe disagreements between Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eizenkot have darkened the prospects of forming a national unity government in Israel. He added Netanyahu and his allies have raised issues of election fraud, Arab party participation, and the military threat of the Islamic Republic, but distrust between the two factions remains an obstacle to agreement. Amir also said Naftali Bennett may negotiate with Netanyahu and Eizenkot could form a coalition without Arab parties, and a new election is not unlikely.

Iranian media quoted Ali Pourmand, head of the medical committee of the Tehran Football Board, saying that holding any football training or matches in Tehran province on Tuesday, 26 Aban 1405 is prohibited. This comes after football training and matches were also canceled earlier this week in Tehran due to air pollution.

Behnam Taleblu said the Islamic Republic, after recent wars and a reduction in its nuclear capability, seeks to increase nuclear and missile threats against the international community. He added that Tehran is trying to extend the range of its missiles and expand its threats beyond the region. Taleblu considered the summit of the US, Russia, and China leaders related to the formation of a new global order and said Gulf countries seek security guarantees and economic reconstruction and do not fully trust the US strategy.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said the possible decision of Trump to attack the Islamic Republic depends on various factors, including the positions of advisors, Arab countries and Israel, the behavior of the Islamic Republic, the ability to maintain the US military posture in the region, the short time left until the new Congress starts, negotiations with China and Russia, and the consequences of retaliatory attacks by the Islamic Republic.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that the people of Iran are determined to overthrow the Islamic Republic regardless of Trump's decisions or political developments in Israel. He added that the people's expectation from the international community, especially the US and Israel, is to weaken the repression structure so they can achieve their goal with minimal cost and damage.

Donald Trump announced that he will discuss the Islamic Republic, the Ukraine war, and nuclear disarmament with the presidents of China and Russia. At the same time, JD Vance, the US Vice President, said the Trump administration will not allow the war with the Islamic Republic to become a long-term commitment for the United States.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations Center reported receiving a report of an incident 13 kilometers north of Khasab in Oman. According to the report, an oil tanker stopped working after an attack caused a fire in its engine room while passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

Peyman Hadadi, CEO of Persepolis, said that the advertisement for the sale of Amirhossein Mahmoudi in the newspaper was intended to show that there were interested parties and they did not intend to sell him. Hadadi added that any offer for Mahmoudi from Tuesday would be considered inducement, and this was a collective decision by the club's managers. He also said that Mahmoudi has two more seasons left on his contract with Persepolis, his contract is low, but they were seeking to increase it and have rewarded him for his national team call-up.

The Kuwaiti representative at the UN meeting on a Middle East free of weapons of mass destruction rejected the Islamic Republic's positions regarding attacks on US bases in the region and asked whether the residential neighborhoods and civilian facilities in Kuwait that were attacked are also US bases. He considered these positions an obvious attempt to shirk Tehran's responsibility for attacks against the sovereignty and territorial integrity of these countries.

A Turkish defense company has announced the development of a system that can disrupt the operation of dozens of drones simultaneously and within seconds. According to the company, the new system targets the electronic equipment of drones using powerful electromagnetic waves and is part of the "Steel Dome" project, a multi-layered air defense system of Turkey.

The Netherlands national team experienced its worst defeat since 1959 by losing 5-0 to Germany in the UEFA Nations League. This loss is one of the 10 heaviest defeats in Dutch history and the first time in nearly 70 years that the Netherlands lost by five goals or more. Previously, the worst defeat was a 12-2 loss to an amateur England team in 1907.

The New York Times has reported that Commander Alireza Asgari was kidnapped and killed by Mossad twenty years after his disappearance. The killing of Asgari has not yet been proven. His fate remains unclear amid narratives of asylum, espionage, and death in captivity.

Kayhan newspaper reported the secret implementation of a bread rationing plan in Khuzestan and Zanjan provinces, causing crowds at bakeries and verbal conflicts. The monthly ration per person is about eight kilograms of flour at the government rate of 2,300 tomans, and purchases above the limit are calculated at the free market rate of 12,650 tomans. Earlier, Instagram channels reported bread rationing in several cities in Khuzestan, with excess purchases calculated at 13,150 tomans.

CNN reported that Tehran is planning a possible attack with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, but there is no evidence yet of a decision to carry out these plans. The network cited seven US officials saying new intelligence indicates plots targeting senior officials of Donald Trump's administration, but there is disagreement about the Islamic Republic's capability and intent. Sources said these plans are mainly to have various options and do not necessarily mean an imminent attack.

The Dutch newspaper Trouw reported that the Dutch police's special counter-espionage team is investigating the possibility that the order for the failed assassination attempt on Siamak Teddin Tahmasbi, an Iranian journalist and artist, in Khordad 1403 was issued by the Islamic Republic. Judicial sources in the Netherlands have confirmed that officers are trying to determine who ordered the attack on this critic of the Islamic Republic. The investigation is taking place simultaneously with the trial of six suspects involved in the assassination attempt on Teddin Tahmasbi.

JD Vance, Trump's deputy, told Fox News that Trump has many options regarding Iran's nuclear program, including increasing military and diplomatic pressures. He added that the US has achieved many military successes against the Islamic Republic, but some want the Iran war to continue indefinitely.

The New York Times reported, citing experts, that Iran's extensive network of dams and water transfer projects may have been built partly to support underground missile bases. Experts said projects without clear civilian justification could help sustain underground military facilities, but this link remains speculative. Nima Shokri said his group examined the locations of 533 dams and found the pattern of this year's airstrikes closely resembles the distribution of dams.

Al Arabiya reported that an Iranian delegation has entered Baghdad to negotiate reducing tensions between the Iraqi government and the Kata'ib Hezbollah group. The delegation is expected to talk with Iraqi government officials and armed groups to prevent military confrontation. The Iraqi Prime Minister has called for armed groups to withdraw from the Jurf al-Sakhar area and hand over control to official security forces.

Sergei Sobyanin, the mayor of Moscow, announced that about 800 drones were launched towards Moscow overnight, with 321 of them being shot down. Non-Russian official sources have not yet confirmed this information. This attack occurs as US mediation efforts to end the Ukraine war have entered a more intense phase.

Farzin Nadimi, a senior defense and security researcher, referred to a CNN report about the possibility of the Islamic Republic using a dirty bomb in the US and said that making such a bomb is not very difficult with access to radioactive materials, but successfully carrying out an attack with it on US soil is very complex. He warned that if such an attack occurs, the US government's response to the Islamic Republic would be very harsh.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, announced before his trip to Asia that in a trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, he will discuss the war in Ukraine, nuclear disarmament, and the issue of Iran. This meeting is scheduled for Thursday, 28 Aban, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China; however, Reuters reported that the three parties have not yet agreed on the format and agenda.

Hossein Ghazian, a sociologist, said that when survival becomes the main focus of people's lives, competition replaces cooperation and economic pressure can lead to increased domestic violence, street fights, and crime. He added that the rise in depression, suicide, decreased marriage and childbirth, and migration indicates that many people no longer see a bright future ahead of them.

Hossein Vahid Khorasani, a Shia religious authority, died at the age of 105. Earlier on 15 Aban, Iranian media reported his death, but shortly after, his office denied the news and asked people to pray for his health.

Shahram Kholdi, a researcher of Middle Eastern history and international relations, said concerns about terrorist attacks and the use of unconventional weapons could change Washington's calculations. He added that the Islamic Republic will isolate itself more due to the lack of reliable decision-makers for negotiation and agreement.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, emphasized at the London mayor's banquet London's opposition to the Islamic Republic obtaining nuclear weapons and suppressing the Iranian people. He said Britain will not allow threats to the region or attacks on journalists and the Jewish community. He also considered the indefinite continuation of the war contrary to Britain's interests and, referring to its economic consequences, stressed London's support for mediators' efforts to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, warned on Tuesday, 26 Aban, in a message on the social network X, referring to experts' statements in The New York Times about the dual use of dams near the missile bases of the Islamic Republic, about targeting civilian infrastructure near US and Israeli bases. Ghalibaf wrote that the new rule is that any dam, port, or power plant near an American or Israeli base has dual use, and they will apply this logic equally and without discrimination.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, said at the ceremony honoring the 2026 International Science Olympiad medalists that the people deserve a much better life and that we are to blame for the current situation. He added that everyone who knows and can should put their utmost effort forward and that we can repeat our scientific successes in practice as well.

Ahmad Vahidi, commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, said at a ceremony at the burial site of Ruhollah Khomeini that Iran does not need any country and that God is with Iran. He added that everyone is in the grip of the power of the Islamic Republic and the country is ready for another great transformation. Vahidi also said that the US is in unprecedented isolation and that the Iranian nation will never bow to arrogance and Israel.

Peyman Hadadi, CEO of Persepolis, announced that the club has taken its complaint about the status of Yaser Asani, Esteghlal player, to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) and intends to pursue the case to the end. Hadadi said they have taken Asani's case to CAS and will continue until the end. He also emphasized that even if Asani's status is confirmed by FIFA President Gianni Infantino, the complaint will continue.

Al Hadath reported, citing Bahrain TV, that Bahrain's air defense systems are countering air attacks from the Islamic Republic. The IRGC public relations announced that on the early morning of Tuesday, 26 Aban, IRGC combat drones targeted a US radar system at Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain. The IRGC stated this action was in response to continued violations of the Islamic Republic's airspace by US military drones.

The Pakistani foreign minister, after meeting with Abbas Araghchi, stated that Islamabad has not stopped its efforts to resume talks between Tehran and Washington. He considered the Islamabad memorandum of understanding as the only way to resolve the conflict between the Islamic Republic and the US.

Hossein Alizadeh said that after the failure of mediation efforts by Qatar, Turkey, and Pakistan, Muscat may be testing a new path for dialogue between Tehran and Washington. He considered managing tensions in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz as probable goals of these consultations. Alizadeh also said the issue of war with the Islamic Republic is still unresolved for the US.

UEFA on Monday, 25 Aban, introduced Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation, as a rival to Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election scheduled for March 18, 2027, in Rabat. UEFA's executive committee and FIFA council members expressed full support for Diallo. After repeated refusals from other figures, UEFA finally chose Philippe Diallo as a credible candidate.

Videos released on social media show the funeral ceremony of Sogand Sayadi, a 16-year-old student, in Gilan-e Gharb on Monday, 25 Aban. Sogand died suspiciously in Kermanshah on 23 Aban. Multiple reports have been published about domestic violence against her and negligence by school officials regarding her situation.

The Israeli parliament is voting on the election of Matan Kahana, a representative of the Yesh Atid party, as the new speaker of the Knesset. It is predicted that he will gain the majority of votes with the support of the Gadi Eisenkot coalition and Arab parties.
On Wednesday, 13 Aban, Leila Goli, who was a victim of child marriage, was killed by her ex-husband with a cold weapon in Shahin Dezh county.

Mohammad Darvish, an environmental expert, criticized officials for neglecting the air pollution problem, calling budget shortages an excuse and saying officials prioritize sending a monkey to space over solving urban issues. He also pointed to the continued use of mazut in power plants and said this practice will likely increase until the end of winter.

On Monday, 25 Aban, Mustafa Qaderi, Seyed Mohammad Saleh Hosseini, Hossein Abdollahi, and Khaled Rahimi, citizens from Saqez, were released on bail. Meanwhile, Mohammad Hakimpour remains in detention.

Financial statements of Persepolis Club show that its net loss for the fiscal year ending 31 Khordad 1405 increased by 81% compared to the previous year, reaching over 1,113 billion tomans. This loss is mainly due to operating expenses exceeding revenues, increased administrative and financial costs, and a sharp decline in other revenues. Persepolis' operating income grew by 61% to about 915 billion tomans, but direct costs exceeded 1,526 billion tomans.

A group singing the song "Ghesseye Eshgh" by Ebi in the teaser of the music program "Sahneh" sparked reactions from government-affiliated media. Tasnim News Agency claimed the program lacks a broadcasting license and did not follow production regulations. Filimo announced the program is scheduled to be released on 9 Azar.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, stated in an interview with Fox News that the Trump administration will not allow a war with the Islamic Republic to continue for years. He said Trump has multiple options to confront Iran's nuclear program, including increasing military and diplomatic pressures.

Mobin Hosseini, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Sari, was arrested after being summoned and appearing at the city's prosecutor's office on Tuesday, 26 Aban. His interrogation session was held at the General and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office of Sari, where he faced charges including "propaganda against the regime" and was arrested after the session ended.

Videos received by Iran International show that Iranians living in Hamburg, Germany, gathered and lit candles on Monday, 25 Aban, in memory of Kian Pirfalak. Kian, a 9-year-old child, was killed by agents of the Islamic Republic on 25 Aban 1401 during the Mahsa uprising.

Sadegh Nojouki, the composer of the song "Ghesseye Eshgh," expressed dissatisfaction with the use of this song in the teaser of the music competition "Sahneh" in an interview with Iran International and said he will pursue the matter legally. The duet of this song by Ebi in the teaser has sparked reactions from government media; his works have been removed from official Islamic Republic media for decades.

German media reported that Berlin police began raids on 28 locations linked to the mosque association "Al-Ershad" on Tuesday, 26 Aban, following the ban on its activities due to accusations of supporting Lebanon's Hezbollah. The Berlin State Interior Minister stated that the ban was due to financial and promotional support for Hezbollah and the association's activities conflicting with German criminal laws. Public use of the association's symbols is banned and its assets have been seized.

Multiple messages have been received by Iran International indicating the sudden and unannounced implementation of a bread rationing plan in several provinces, including Zanjan and Khuzestan. Citizens report crowds in front of bakeries and concerns about bread supply.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, referred to a New York Times report about the possibility of targeting Iran's dams and said that attacks on dams and water facilities are severely restricted and almost prohibited under the Additional Protocol of the Geneva Convention due to their consequences for civilians. He added that with rising tensions between the Islamic Republic and the US, the possibility of targeting Iran's critical infrastructure, including power plants and water facilities, has been raised, but so far US officials have not taken a position on attacking dams.

Cristiano Ronaldo, the Portuguese star of Al Nassr Saudi Arabia, started a symbolic countdown to reach the record of 1,000 goals in his professional football career by posting a video on his Instagram page. He has scored 985 official goals in club and national competitions and is 15 goals away from reaching 1,000 goals. Ronaldo, who has played for Sporting Lisbon, Manchester United, Real Madrid, and Juventus, currently plays for Al Nassr Saudi Arabia and is aiming to set one of the most important individual records of his career.

Seyed Ali Kazemi, spokesperson for the judiciary, announced the confirmation of the death sentence for one of the detainees related to the December 1404 protests in Rasht. He claimed that this individual was involved in attacking and setting fire to several public and medical centers in the city. The issued sentence was confirmed by Branch 39 of the Supreme Court.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing severe air pollution in Tehran and said the government is unable to manage the situation and must go.
